summary: The core reuses the Contra K007121 engine. It renders as a scan-time pipeline: per-line tile and sprite fetch state machines feed line buffers, interrupts come off raster-counter bits, and the 7-bit COA-style colour output goes to an external palette RAM. None of this follows the structure of MAME's frame-based tilemap/sprites_draw. The flkatck-specific glue (an address-line gate on the gfx ROM bus, extra latch bits for board nets, a palette RAM read twice per pixel) also departs from MAME's hacks and abstractions. Register semantics and the I/O decode necessarily match MAME, so the evidence leans hardware without being strongly so.

findings.signal: Scan-time sprite engine, not MAME's per-frame block loop
findings.note: Sprites are evaluated again on every HS edge for the current vrender line. Bytes are fetched one at a time by stepping scan_base by 5, and the scan stops at a y==240 terminator, scan_base 0x13b, or a 384-pixel budget per line. MAME instead pre-counts 264 sprite blocks and draws whole sprites with its x_offset/y_offset tables, which do not appear in the HDL.

findings.signal: Sprite code/size built from bits, no MAME tables
findings.note: Sub-tile selection drives code[3:0] directly from vsub bits, hflip and size_attr bits, much like ROM address lines. MAME instead masks the number and adds entries from offset tables.

findings.signal: Tilemap rendered per line into double line buffer
findings.note: An 8-state FSM fetches attribute and code from VRAM for each 8-pixel column of the next line, then writes 9-bit pixels into a ping-pong line buffer. On wide-layout lines it makes a second 'scores' pass. MAME uses two tilemap objects, cached tile_info callbacks and clip rectangles.

NMI fires on edges of vdump[4] or vdump[5], selected by nmi_pace. IRQ fires on the LVBL falling edge, and FIRQ toggles on every other IRQ. All of these come from the raster counter rather than from a scanline-timer callback.

findings.signal: Board-logic gating on gfx ROM address
findings.note: Upper ROM address bits are forced to zero when pre_gfx1_addr[13:10]==0 and the fetch is for tiles. This is address-line gating like discrete glue logic, and it replaces MAME's ad-hoc 'attr==0x0d && scroll==0' bank hack.

findings.signal: Second chip dropped, palette bits taken from colour output
findings.note: The palette RAM address is assembled from the chip's tile/sprite select bit, palette nibble and pixel nibble, with BYPASS_VPROM/OPROM standing in for the absent PROMs. MAME uses a palette_device colour index (+16 offset).

findings.signal: 8-bit palette RAM read twice per pixel
findings.note: A byte-wide palette RAM is read twice per pixel, with pal_half as the address LSB and the bytes shifted together into 15-bit RGB, the way a board with an 8-bit colour RAM would do it. MAME's palette device does this conversion abstractly.

findings.signal: Latch bits for board nets that MAME ignores
findings.note: The bank-register write latches bits 7..5 into net_wowr, net_nrd and net_end, named after board nets. MAME uses only bits 0-1 for the bank and bits 3-4 for coin counters, and also has a '!=3 for safety' guard that the HDL does not copy.

findings.signal: I/O decode matches MAME's ls138 handlers
findings.note: The case on A[4:2] matches MAME's (offset&0x1c)>>2 switch. Both are the memory map a correct core must share, so this points neither way.

findings.signal: Register semantics mirror MAME's documented ctrl regs
findings.note: The mmr fields and the bank-bit selection (attr[3+codeN_sel], with mask/extra bits from reg 4) follow the same per-register decomposition MAME uses. This is mostly necessary shared behaviour, with at most a slight MAME flavour.

findings.signal: 007452 as a serial divider, 7-bit factor A
findings.note: The divider is a cycle-by-cycle restoring divider, and factor A is only 7 bits. MAME computes dividend/divisor in one step, uses an 8-bit factor and special-cases a zero divisor. The behaviour differs from MAME in the way a reverse-engineered chip would.
